Twitter: @anthonyfenech
From: Thomas, Christopher <cdthomas@freepress.com>
Sent: Thursday, August 22, 2019 11:30:27 PM
To: Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>
Subject: Fenech 
 
It was avoidable and inexcusable.

The Houston Astros knowingly violated the collective bargaining agreement – which actually is designed to protect ballplayers -- when the franchise blocked Free Press writer Anthony Fenech from entering their clubhouse with Houston media on Wednesday night.
Justin Verlander, arguably the greatest pitcher in Tigers history, refused to talk to any reporters if Fenech was present.  So, the Astros made sure Fenech was absent.
Players have no obligation to talk to every media member in a postgame scrum. They can ignore questions. They can give non-answers.
But the league says reporters must have access.
The Astros know this. They just didn’t care.

Instead, they asked three security officials to guard the entrance to the clubhouse while Verlander spoke to reporters on the other side of the door. Six minutes later, the guards allowed Fenech to pass. By then, Verlander’s media availability was done.
If that sounds harsh, it is.
If that sounds like punishment, it is.
If that sounds embarrassing, it is.
Major League Baseball must take action.
Chris Thomas
Sports editor, Detroit Free Press
Great Lakes regional sports director, USA TODAY Network
cdthomas@freepress.com
@bychristhomas
